newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa waits on $200 mln Yankee bond.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa waits on $200 mln Yankee bond.

text.p: Mexican steel firm Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) is ready to issue a $200 million Yankee bond, but is waiting for market conditions to improve, a company executive said on Monday.
"We are ready, but we don't expect market conditions to improve for at least 60 days," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The deal is part of a jumbo strategy by Ahmsa to refinance its debts to achieve lower rates and longer maturities. Ahmsa's liabilities were around $1.5 billion at the end of 1996.

The source said the issue could pay a maximum of 9.5 or 10 percent -- not a major difference from its current interest cost. However, the benefit of a Yankee bond is that it extends maturities to some seven or 10 years, he noted.

Merrill Lynch and Santander are expected to lead manage the bond, which will be issued in addition to the $330 million export-backed credit already negotiated by lead manager J.P. Morgan. That two-tranche deal is expected to hit the markets within days.
Ahmsa's refinancing efforts are expected to shave some 70 basis points off its average debt servicing costs, and extend the average maturity to six years from 4.5 years, the source said.
